audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed with its own reasoning text and with the packet chart in four of seven rows (0, 1, 2, 6).
audit.why: whys[0] describes Riven poking a Galio with only Winds of War, yet win[0] said 'Skill'. whys[1] says neither side has a decisive edge, yet win[1] said 'Riven'. whys[2] says Galio wins the trade outright, yet win[2] said 'Riven'. whys[6] says the 1v1 window closes, yet win[6] said 'Riven'. Packet levelChart reads Riven / Skill / Galio / Skill / Galio / Riven / Skill.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 6 flipped to Riven / Skill / Galio / Skill, proposed as matched full+content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] named Immortal Shieldbow as the first-item spike while every other string on the page builds Eclipse, and the Level 6 why blamed a 'Level 5 combo'.
audit.why: The item spike must match the build the page recommends, and the Level 6 row is about Blade of the Exile arming Wind Slash, not a Level 5 combo.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] rebuilt around Eclipse plus Justice Punch's 11s cooldown; whys[4] rewritten around Blade of the Exile vs Shield of Durand's 18s taunt.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] attributed a '13-second cooldown' to Justice Punch. Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7. 13 seconds is Riven's own Broken Wings cooldown.
audit.why: The whole win condition is punishing Galio's dash while it is down; a wrong number by two seconds is the difference between a free all-in and eating a knockup mid-chain.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 11 seconds, and Shield of Durand named by its Riot name with its real 18s rank-1 cooldown as the second gate on committing.

audit.why: Justice Punch is correctly identified as the punishable cooldown; only the number was wrong, fixed under point 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file tags Galio's E with a 'terrain' flag ('creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes').
audit.why: Riot's own description of Justice Punch is a backstep-and-charge knockup with no terrain creation, so the derived flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire. Per instructions the description wins.
audit.corrected: No terrain claim written to the page; recorded here and in notes instead.

edits.before: Galio has no Justice Punch at Level 1 — Q-auto-Q poke him freely and build an HP lead before his knockup dash is available.
edits.after: Galio has only Winds of War at Level 1, and it costs 60 mana — Q-auto-Q between tornadoes and bank an HP lead before Justice Punch.

edits.before: Both kits are fully online but the lane is still about tracking Justice Punch; neither of you has a decisive edge in a clean trade yet.
edits.after: At two he picks Justice Punch or the taunt and you pick W or E; neither second ability decides a clean trade, so save your dash for his step-up.

edits.before: Galio's Justice Punch into W taunt absorbs your all-in — if you run the combo into a ready Galio, he wins the trade and you burn E for nothing.
edits.after: Justice Punch into Shield of Durand absorbs your all-in — commit into a ready Galio and he taunts you mid-chain. That taunt is 18s at rank 1.

edits.before: Galio's W taunt plus Justice Punch is at its most dangerous here — he can absorb your whole Level 5 combo and trade back through damage reduction; respect it.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile arms Wind Slash, but Shield of Durand eats the burst — pop R after his taunt, not before, and execute him once it is on its 18s cooldown.

edits.before: Immortal Shieldbow spike gives you enough burst and sustain to all-in past his W taunt; track Justice Punch and run the kill window the moment it misses or expires.
edits.after: Your Eclipse spike gives enough burst to all-in through Shield of Durand; track Justice Punch's 11s cooldown and run the kill window the moment it misses.

edits.before: Bait Justice Punch into the wave, then E-Q3-W burst him while the 13-second cooldown is running
edits.after: Bait Justice Punch into the wave, then E-Q3-W burst him while its 11-second cooldown is running

edits.before: Activate W taunt to absorb your all-in damage behind percentage damage reduction
edits.after: Charge Shield of Durand to taunt you and absorb the all-in behind damage reduction

notes: The packet's two suspectNames here ('Hit Justice Punch', "Justice Punch's") are FALSE POSITIVES — Justice Punch is the correct Riot name for Galio's E. Galio's E carries a derived 'terrain' flag that contradicts Riot's own description (a backstep-and-charge knockup, no terrain); treated as a parsing misfire and not written to the page. Full-layer prose (phases[N].why, breakdown.*, report[N].t, tldr, tradeGood) is stored with mojibake em dashes (â€”) in this brief, so I did not risk retyping those before-strings; the full-layer prose still says 'Full kit online — your core pattern starts now' on the Level 3 row that now reads Galio, and that why line should be re-pointed by a pass that can copy the exact bytes off disk. Level 6 (row 4) left as 'Skill' despite the packet saying 'Galio': Galio's Hero's Entrance needs an ally to land on and does nothing in a top-lane 1v1, while Riven gains AD, range and Wind Slash, so 'Galio' would be a claim I cannot support.
